question: What did Franke and Kaul find about the variables explaining output in the Hawthorne experiments?

injection.why: Nothing in this corpus can be OUTDATED naturally: the oldest node is ~4 days old against a 30-day threshold. Ageing one retrieved node past the threshold is the only way to exercise the branch.
injection.cypher: MATCH (e:Topic {name:'Economic Depression As Positive Factor In Production'}) SET e.created_at = datetime() - duration({days:400}), e.updated_at = datetime() - duration({days:400}), e.injected = true

expected_behavior: The aggregate status must become OUTDATED (worst-case across sources) and the gate must FAIL, because OUTDATED is in KG_FAILING_STATUSES. Also a regression test for the string timestamp bug: before conversion, created_at was STRING, to_datetime() returned None, and this node would have been reported VALID no matter how old it was.

question: What are the three dimensions of supply chain integration studied by Flynn et al.?

injection.why: The graph has 0 SUPERSEDED_BY / SUPERSEDES / CONTRADICTS edges, so the supersession branch has never once been executed against real data.
injection.cypher: MATCH (a:Topic {name:'Customer Integration Measurement Framework'}), (b:Topic {name:'Supplier Integration Measurement Framework'}) MERGE (a)-[r:SUPERSEDED_BY]->(b) SET r.injected = true, a.injected = true

expected_behavior: Status must become SUPERSEDED and the gate must FAIL. KG_SUPERSEDES_REL is SUPERSEDED_BY, so the edge direction matters: a is the superseded node.

question: What is the relationship between supply chain integration and performance according to Flynn et al.?

injection.why: Topic.name is currently unique across all 1531 nodes (0 duplicates), so the CONFLICTED branch cannot fire. Injecting a same-name node with a DIFFERENT description satisfies the check under either setting of KG_CONFLICT_REQUIRES_DIFF_DESC. NOTE: this is why topic_name_unique must NOT be applied as a constraint - it would make this item impossible.
injection.cypher: MATCH (o:Topic {name:'Impact Of Supply Chain Integration On Performance'}) CREATE (n:Topic {name:o.name, id:o.id + '_conflict', description:'Integration shows no relationship with performance.', source_type:'paper', confidence_score:0.5, created_at:datetime(), injected:true, conflict_variant:'B'})

expected_behavior: Covers the OTHER route to CONFLICTED, which T03 no longer exercises: two Topic nodes asserting the same name with different descriptions (find_conflicting_ids). That is a structural signal - 'one of these is probably wrong' - whereas T03's contradiction is semantic - 'a classifier read both claims and judged them incompatible'. Both must keep working; they are not interchangeable. Still needs injection because Topic.name is unique across all 3157 nodes, which is also why topic_name_unique must never be applied as a constraint.

injection.why: Aggregation test: ONE stale source among many fresh ones. _aggregate_status takes the worst status by severity, so a single OUTDATED node must dominate a majority of VALID ones. Run this WITHOUT T01's injection applied, so exactly one node in the retrieved set is stale.
injection.cypher: MATCH (e:Topic {name:'First Relay Assembly Test Room At Western Electric'}) SET e.created_at = datetime() - duration({days:120}), e.updated_at = datetime() - duration({days:120}), e.injected = true

expected_behavior: Same question as T01 but only one source is stale. Verifies the aggregate is worst-case rather than majority-vote: if the report comes back VALID because most sources are fresh, the temporal layer is diluted by exactly the nodes it should be protecting against.

question: What did Franke and Kaul find about the variables explaining output in the Hawthorne experiments?

injection.why: With source_type='paper' every node scores ~0.486, so the trust gate now passes everywhere and cannot be observed failing. Dropping confidence_score on the Topics of one paper isolates a trust-only failure: temporal stays VALID, faithfulness is untouched, and trust alone decides.
injection.cypher: MATCH (c:Chunk)-[:MENTIONS]->(e:Topic) WHERE c.filename STARTS WITH 'Franke_1978' SET e.confidence_score = 0.05, e.injected = true

expected_behavior: trust = 0.05 x 1.0 x ~0.97 = ~0.05, far below the 0.4 gate, while temporal stays VALID. The gate must FAIL on trust alone. Also exercises a path the verifier treats specially: a trust-only failure is NOT retryable (re-retrieving the same low-trust graph cannot help), so `retries` must be 0 - unlike a faithfulness failure, which does retry.
